result: There is a specific silence that exists only before dawn, a heavy, suspended moment when the world feels paused. It is not empty, but full of potential energy waiting to be released. When the sun has not yet broken the jagged horizon, dust motes dance in the long beams of streetlights. The coffee machine gurgles softly, the only sound in the room. I sit in this grey light, my mind uncluttered by the demands of the day. There are no emails, no notifications buzzing against the wrist, no expectations screaming for attention. Just me and the drifting thought. Time slows down here. It is a gift we rarely accept. We chase clocks all day, measuring productivity in seconds, but here, time evaporates. It is peaceful in a way that feels almost sacred. I wonder if others feel this connection when the world is asleep. The birds have not started their chorus yet. The air is crisp against the skin. My breath leaves me like a small, white cloud, visible only in the dim room. It is a moment of pure existence without performance or masks. I drink the coffee. It is bitter and hot, waking the body from its slumber. I walk to the window. The street outside is empty, save for an occasional car passing, headlights slicing through the dark before disappearing. Then, the sun rises finally. The spell breaks, but I keep the quiet inside me. That tiny window of nothingness is enough fuel to face the noise.
